source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 2 (Acids, Bases and Salts).

sections.heading: 1. Acids and Bases — Properties
points: **Acids** — sour taste, turn blue litmus red, release **H⁺ (H₃O⁺) ions** in water (e.g. HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, citric, acetic acid).
**Bases** — bitter, soapy feel, turn red litmus blue, release **OH⁻ ions** in water; soluble bases = **alkalis** (NaOH, KOH, Ca(OH)₂).
**Indicators** show acid/base: litmus, methyl orange, phenolphthalein; **olfactory indicators** (onion, vanilla, clove) change smell.
Acids/bases conduct electricity in solution (release ions) — proves ionisation.

sections.heading: 2. Reactions of Acids and Bases
points: **Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen gas** (pop test) (e.g. Zn + H₂SO₄).
**Acid + metal carbonate/bicarbonate → salt + water + CO₂** (turns lime water milky).
**Base + metal → salt + hydrogen** (e.g. Zn + NaOH).
**Neutralisation:** acid + base → salt + water (e.g. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O).
Dilution: acids/bases dissolve in water release heat — **always add acid to water** (never the reverse) to avoid splattering.

sections.heading: 3. pH Scale and Its Importance
points: **pH scale** (0–14) measures H⁺ concentration: **pH < 7 = acidic**, **pH = 7 = neutral**, **pH > 7 = basic**.
Strong acids/bases fully ionise; weak ones partly.

sub: Body: our body works within pH 7.0–7.8; **stomach acid (HCl)** aids digestion; **antacids** (mild base) relieve acidity.
Soil pH affects crops; tooth decay when mouth pH < 5.5 (toothpaste is basic).
Bee/ant sting = acidic (relieved by baking soda); nettle sting acidic.

sections.heading: 4. Salts and Common Chemicals
points: **Salts** — from acids and bases; family by parent acid/base; solutions can be acidic, basic or neutral.
**Common salt (NaCl)** → raw material for NaOH (chlor-alkali process gives NaOH, Cl₂, H₂).
**Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂)** — from Cl₂ + Ca(OH)₂; used for bleaching, disinfecting water.
**Baking soda (NaHCO₃)** — antacid, in baking (with tartaric acid = baking powder), fire extinguishers.
**Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O)** — cleaning, glass/soap/paper industry; **Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O)** from gypsum — casts, ceilings.
**Water of crystallisation** = fixed water molecules in a salt (e.g. copper sulphate CuSO₄·5H₂O — blue).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Acids release H⁺; bases release OH⁻; alkalis = soluble bases.
pH < 7 acidic, 7 neutral, >7 basic; tooth decay below pH 5.5.
Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen (pop test); always add acid to water.
Bleaching powder = CaOCl₂; baking soda = NaHCO₃; washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
Plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O (from gypsum); blue vitriol = CuSO₄·5H₂O.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Always add acid to water** (dilution is exothermic).
**pH decreases → more acidic**; tooth decay starts below **pH 5.5**.
**Baking soda = NaHCO₃**; **washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O** (do not confuse).
**Plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O** (half water molecule).
